extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models as embodied brain for robotic manipulation, covering 5 dimensions (instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis), 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang; State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Institute for Brain and Intelligence, Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.citeAs: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang. (2025). RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.17801v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: RoboBench constructs datasets from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection. The benchmark includes data across single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T, Open X-Embodiment, RoboCasa, RoboMIND, and others, combined with in-house collected robotic manipulation videos across diverse embodiments.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing includes frame extraction from robotic videos, standardization into multiple-choice QA format, template-based QA generation, and filtering based on image quality and task validity. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules—such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are generated through a combination of MLLM-based automatic annotation (using Gemini for structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata) and human expert refinement. Human annotators refine MLLM outputs and provide ground truth labels for specific tasks such as bounding boxes, affordance points, and failure cases.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Gemini (for video segmentation and structured annotations), GPT (for functional properties generation), human annotators (for refinement and quality control)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. After data construction, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple annotations per item: video frames annotated with task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), bounding boxes, affordance points/trajectories, and failure labels. Human annotators validate and refine MLLM-generated annotations through majority-vote strategy.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for video segmentation, structured annotation generation including task summaries and step-wise instructions), GPT (for functional property generation and implicit instruction conversion), Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark acknowledges potential biases from the nature of existing planning data, which primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left–right arm assignments or positional movements. This may affect dual-arm coordination and mobile manipulation evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) difficulties with implicit instruction comprehension, (2) weak spatiotemporal reasoning and limited embodiment awareness, (3) struggles with dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning, (4) shallow affordance prediction capabilities, and (5) execution-level failure diagnosis remains extremely challenging even for human evaluators.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating MLLMs as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across five key dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It serves as a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.

name.evidence: We introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains.

description.evidence: RoboBench defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Experiments on 14 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal fundamental limitations: difficulties with implicit instruction comprehension, spatiotemporal reasoning, cross-scenario planning, fine-grained affordance understanding, and execution failure diagnosis... Finally, execution-level failure diagnosis remains the hardest dimension, with scores of 10–20 compared to 40–60 on planning error analysis, and even human evaluators achieving only 47.30, underscoring the intrinsic difficulty.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence... RoboBench thus provides a unified scaffold for measuring embodied cognition and guiding the development of more robust, generalizable embodied intelligence.
